\chapter{Communication Complexity — Minimax}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.CommunicationComplexity.NewmanTheorem.Minimax
\section{Overview}

This module establishes Yao's minimax principle for public-coin communication complexity.
It introduces the distributional error of a deterministic protocol under an input
distribution, proves a Fubini-type integral-swap lemma, and derives the key one-direction
minimax bound: if every deterministic protocol of complexity at most $n$ errs with
probability greater than $\varepsilon$ under some distribution $\mu$ on $X \times Y$,
then the public-coin randomized communication complexity of $f$ at error $\varepsilon$
exceeds $n$.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Distributional error of a deterministic protocol]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.distributionalError}
\statementsource{roughgarden-cc-bootcamp}{pdf-d54d402b16e2-p013-b004}
\statementsource{roughgarden-cc-oneway}{
  pdf-043896d6545f-p012-b003,
  pdf-043896d6545f-p012-b004
}
\statementsource{raoyehudayoff-ch03-randomized-protocols}{pdf-3eebfb23ab53-p004-b001}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.distributionalError}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.run, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace}
Given a deterministic protocol $p : \mathrm{Protocol}\,X\,Y\,\alpha$, a finite
probability space $\mu$ on $X \times Y$, and a target function $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$,
the \emph{distributional error} $p.\mathrm{distributionalError}(\mu, f) \in \mathbb{R}$
is the $\mu$-probability that the output of $p$ disagrees with $f$, i.e.\
$\mu\bigl(\{(x,y) \mid p.\mathrm{run}(x,y) \ne f(x,y)\}\bigr)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Swapping input and coin averages of the failure probability]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.failureIntegral_swap}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.failureIntegral_swap}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.CoinTape, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace.measureReal_eq_integral_indicator_one, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.Protocol.rrun}
\difficulty{5}
Suppose $X\times Y$ is a finite probability space, whose probability measure we write
$\mathbb{P}$, let $m\in\bbn$, and let $p$ be a public-coin protocol whose shared
randomness is a coin tape in $\mathrm{CoinTape}(m)$, with Alice's private input drawn
from $X$, Bob's from $Y$, and outputs in $\alpha$. Write $\mathrm{vol}$ for the measure
on $\mathrm{CoinTape}(m)$, and for a coin tape $\omega$ and inputs $x,y$ let
$\mathrm{rrun}(p,x,y,\omega)$ be the randomized execution of $p$. Then for every
function $f\colon X\times Y\to\alpha$,
\[
\int_{\mathrm{CoinTape}(m)} \mathbb{P}\!\left(\bigl\{(x,y)\in X\times Y :
\mathrm{rrun}(p,x,y,\omega)\neq f(x,y)\bigr\}\right)\,d\omega
=
\int_{X\times Y} \mathrm{vol}\!\left(\bigl\{\omega\in\mathrm{CoinTape}(m) :
\mathrm{rrun}(p,x,y,\omega)\neq f(x,y)\bigr\}\right)\,d\mathbb{P}(x,y).
\]
On the left one first measures, for each fixed coin tape $\omega$, the
$\mathbb{P}$-probability of the inputs on which $p$ disagrees with $f$, and then
averages over $\omega$; on the right one first measures, for each fixed input pair
$(x,y)$, the set of coin tapes on which $p$ disagrees with $f$, and then averages over
the inputs.
\end{lemma}

\uses{CommunicationComplexity.CoinTape, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.complexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.distributionalError, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace.integral_le_of_le, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace.lt_integral_of_lt, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.Protocol.rrun, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.Protocol.toDeterministic, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.Protocol.toDeterministic_run, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity_le_iff, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.failureIntegral_swap}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be a target function, let $\varepsilon \in \bbr$, let $n
\in \bbn$, and let $\mu$ be a finite probability space on $X \times Y$. Suppose that
every deterministic protocol $p$ whose communication complexity is at most $n$ has
distributional error strictly greater than $\varepsilon$ against $f$ under $\mu$; that
is, the $\mu$-probability that $p$ disagrees with $f$ exceeds $\varepsilon$. Then the
$\varepsilon$-error public-coin randomized communication complexity of $f$ is strictly
greater than $n$.
\end{theorem}
